ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$, where $BC = 7$ and $EC = 4$. What is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$,\\
it follows that $BC=EF=7$,\\
thus, $CF=EF-EC=7-4=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, points B, E, C, F are on the same horizontal line, arranged in order from left to right. The base of triangle ABC is BC, and the base of triangle DEF is EF; point C is located between E and F, so EC is a part of EF, and CF is the remaining segment of EF. Reasoning: It is known that \(\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF\); according to the corresponding order of vertices, side \(BC\) corresponds to side \(EF\). Therefore \(EF = BC = 7\). Also because \(EF = EC + CF\), and \(EC = 4\), therefore \(CF = 7 - 4 = 3\).
